comment: Verification contract for T-005 (medium, acceptance-first -- risk-gate-matrix.md's medium-tier row; tdd is reserved for high/critical), originally authored 2026-08-23 because T-005 reached Status: Implementation Complete (commit 472579a3, 2026-08-19) without ever being given this file. UPDATED same-day, second pass: the gap this contract's own first pass found (below) is now closed. Every field below is transcribed from tasks.md's own T-005 block (Risk: medium, Required Workflow: acceptance-first, Requirements: REQ-001/REQ-004/REQ-005/REQ-006/REQ-008) and reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-005.md, never copied from T-003/T-004's own contract structure beyond shape-as-template. Every command this contract cites as evidence was RE-RUN against the current HEAD (febf7898, working tree with this pass's own uncommitted diff) rather than trusted from the implementation report: bash tests/resolve-project-context-match.tests.sh and pwsh -File tests/resolve-project-context-match.tests.ps1 both reproduced 59 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 (verification/qg/T-005/focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log) -- grown from the first pass's own 37/0 by 22 new assertions (two new TEST-056 fixtures). requirement-traceability was performed manually and is NOT recorded as a contract check (medium tier does not require it; check-contract.py's RISK_TIERS['medium'] omits requirement-traceability), but its own findings are load-bearing and recorded in verification/qg/T-005/traceability.log. GAP CLOSED, NOT SMOOTHED OVER: this contract's own first pass found T-005's own Done When item 2 ('Byte-identity / aggregation / provenance locks') unmet because TEST-056 (AC-056, diagnostics[] warn/block cardinality) had no fixture, assertion, or reference anywhere in this task's own suite -- root-caused to a genuine, unimplemented production-code gap in resolve-project-context.py's own _write_evidence (hardcoded severity: 'block' unconditionally; contracts/resolver-evidence.schema.json's own severity enum already permitted 'warn'). That production code is T-004's own scope (Resolver Evidence assembly, REQ-004 share; tasks.md's own T-004 Requirements text names AC-056 among the production behavior T-004's own code must implement, even though T-005 owns the dedicated test suite) -- T-004 was Implementation Complete, not Done, at the time this gap was found, so completing a behavior T-004's own Goal/Scope already declared it owns is T-004's own completion work, not a reopening of finished scope or a frozen-spec amendment; T-005's own Out of Scope ('this task never edits resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} itself') was not touched by T-005's own diff. T-004 extended _evaluate_capabilities/_write_evidence/_block (see T-004's own contract/report for the full account); T-005 then authored TEST-056 (two fixtures -- one reusing REQ-006 item (d)'s own existing dsl-warn-unmatched-trigger fixture verbatim, one a new multi-node fixture -- against the corrected engine, TDD RED->GREEN even though acceptance-first does not require it: verification/T-005/red-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log (55 passed / 4 failed, captured in an isolated git-clone scratch copy at this branch's own committed pre-fix HEAD, never reverting the real worktree), verification/T-005/green-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log (59/0). Two directional mutation kills confirmed in the same scratch clone: emitting a second summary entry is caught by the 'exactly one summary severity:block entry, never a second' assertion in both fixtures; collapsing the per-node warn entries into one is caught by the multi-node fixture's own 'exactly 3 severity:warn entries, one per outcome:warn node, never fewer' assertion (the single-node fixture correctly stays green under this second mutation). unit-tests and acceptance-tests are therefore now recorded passes:true, each with red_evidence pointing at this pass's own genuine RED capture (not the original, TEST-056-blind red-{sh,ps1}.log, which is retained untouched at its own original path for historical continuity) and green_evidence at the current 59/0 re-run. check-contract.py is therefore now EXPECTED to report this contract PASSED. regression (verification/qg/T-005/regression.log) re-ran: git diff --stat/status --short against plugins/ (empty -- T-005 is test-only and never edits resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} itself, AC-032), git diff --check (clean), py_compile on the test driver (clean), the T-001 sibling resolver-evidence-schema suite as an incidental-breakage check (20/20 PASS), the upstream block suite re-run as a dependency-side non-regression check (141/0 both runtimes), and the FULL tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 sequence run detached with no deadline per this session's own explicit instruction: sh reports exactly 2 failing suite(s) (deterministic-lane-selfcheck.tests.sh, design-system-contract.tests.sh), ps1 reports exactly 1 (design-system-contract.tests.ps1 -- deterministic-lane-selfcheck has no PowerShell twin at all, a pre-existing structural asymmetry, not a regression this task's diff touches); both self-declare DESIGNED-RED for a documented pre-existing reason and match this repository's own standing baseline exactly, and this task's own new suite is confirmed registered and green inside that same full run. regression is therefore recorded passes:true. Stack: shell waives lint/typecheck/build -- this task ships only stdlib-only Python test drivers plus sh/ps1 dispatcher twins and no compile toolchain is configured for any of the three. check-component-coverage is correctly ABSENT (RISK_TIERS['medium'] does not name it at all -- unlike T-003/T-004's own high tier). task-state-check and check-workflow-state.sh (a separate, non-contract gate) were both independently re-verified and unaffected by this contract's own authoring: check-task-state.sh returns 'Task state check passed for 10 task(s).' exit 0, and check-workflow-state.sh both with and without --feature epic-193-a5-capability-resolver returns 'workflow-state: ok' exit 0 in both modes. Net: this task's own suite is a real, independently-confirmed, 59/0-passing artifact; the gap this contract's own first pass disclosed (TEST-056 unimplemented) is closed, not hidden -- both the closure and the closure's own evidence (RED/GREEN, mutation kills) are recorded above rather than a quiet passes:true flip. GATE CYCLE 1 REMEDIATION (2026-08-23, three Majors from an isolated evaluator, closed same-day): (1) resolver.version/rule_set_revision cross-invocation identity (AC-044 remainder) was previously asserted only by comparing one in-process module load against itself -- invisible to a per-process derivation (the evaluator's own proof: folding os.getpid() into RULE_SET_STRING left 59/0 unchanged) -- two new assertions now spawn the staged .py master as two genuinely separate OS processes and diff the result, plus a structural check that .sh/.ps1 delegate unconditionally to the identical .py and carry no own copy of RESOLVER_VERSION/RULE_SET_REVISION/RULE_SET_STRING; suite grown 59->63 (both runtimes), the evaluator's exact mutant re-injected in a scratch clone now fails at exactly one assertion (resolver-identity-cross-process), 62/1. (2) The persisted red-{sh,ps1}.log (pre-T-004 revert) crashes before reaching any target assertion and demonstrates none of tasks.md's three named defect classes; three NEW scratch-clone captures now do -- red-undermatched-capability-{sh,ps1}.log (M3, union-match any->all, AC-006), red-misaggregated-facet-{sh,ps1}.log (M4, same-Capability duplicate-facet collapse, AC-043/AC-052(b)), and red-noncanonical-provenance-{sh,ps1}.log (this same cycle's own RULE_SET_STRING/os.getpid() mutant) -- each failing for its own stated reason, both runtimes byte-identical per defect class, the real worktree's resolve-project-context.py never touched. red_evidence/green_evidence above now point at red-undermatched-capability-{sh,ps1}.log (most central defect class) and the re-run 63/0 focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log; red-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log remains valid, additive, dedicated AC-056 evidence, not superseded. (3) T-005.md's own '## Outputs' table (first-pass, 20 rows) and '### Outputs (this pass's own additions)' (second-pass, 7 rows) are merged into one '## Outputs' table, re-derived from `git show --name-only` over 472579a3/c6ce6a86/13d5fee0 -- the second-pass rows (red-ac056/green-ac056/warn-cardinality-multi-node fixtures, plus this task's own new T-005.contract.json) were structurally outside the review manifest's own reach (built from the first table only); '## Test Evidence' repointed from the stale 37/0 green-sh.log to the current 63/0 qg/T-005/focused-tests-sh.log. verification/qg/T-005/ logs stay excluded from the Outputs table (T-004.md's own sibling convention for this identical commit set); every row added/removed and why is recorded in the table's own preface note. GATE CYCLE 2 REMEDIATION (2026-08-23, three new Majors from an isolated evaluator, closed same-day): the shared root cause across all three -- "where an expectation is produced by the implementation under test, the assertion is decorative" -- (A) AC-003's byte-identity check: `expected_projection` was `resolver_module._projection(document, source_sha256)`, the SAME function under test computing its own expectation (the evaluator's own proof: mutating every `paths.include` to `MUTANT-WRONG-PATH/**` inside the real resolver subprocess still passed 63/0); it is now literal, hand-transcribed data sharing no code with resolve-project-context.py, and a second new assertion independently recomputes `projection_sha256` by canonicalizing the resolver's own captured projection bytes (never `expected_projection`) and compares the two hashes before use. The mutant re-injected in a fresh scratch clone now fails at exactly two assertions (AC-003 byte-identity and its own projection_sha256 remainder), 63/2. (B) AC-044's `~` escape half: no fixture component id ever contained `~`, so dropping `token.replace("~", "~0")` while keeping the `/` half survived vacuously; `full-pipeline-match/project-context.yaml` now declares a fourth component, `other~thing`, and a dedicated assertion pins its own pointer to `/components/other~0thing`. The evaluator's own drop-the-`~`-rule mutant, re-injected, now fails at that assertion (plus cascading production-side self-validation failures once the pointer is non-canonical), 60/5. (C) AC-043's `solo-never-facet` reason: its own sole contributor, cap-alpha[2], made "names every contributing instance" and "names the first" indistinguishable; `full-pipeline-match/capability-registry.json` now gives cap-beta its own second, always-false `solo-never-facet` declaration (cap-beta[1]), so `reason` must name both. The evaluator's own name-only-the-first mutant, re-injected, now fails at exactly that one assertion, 64/1. MINORS: stale suite-total prose ("59"/"63") corrected to the current 65 throughout this contract and T-005.md; `red-undermatched-capability-{sh,ps1}.log` re-captured -- the identical M3 union-match `any`->`all` mutant no longer crashes the driver with an unguarded KeyError on `cap_alpha_evidence["conditional_facet_evaluations"]` (a key genuinely absent, not empty, when `matched` is False), since that line now reads `.get("conditional_facet_evaluations", [])`; the capture now reaches a clean RESULT line (55/10, exit 1, no traceback). `run_dispatcher_delegation_check`'s own label now matches its own check (both dispatchers' every mention of the delegation target must appear on a real process-launch line, never a bare textual mention -- "unconditionally" is no longer claimed where only substring presence was tested). T-005.md's own '## Outputs' table now ALSO includes `verification/qg/T-005/{focused-tests-sh,focused-tests-ps1,regression,placeholder-scan,task-state}.log` -- gate-cycle-1's own exclusion of these paths (following T-004.md's sibling convention) is itself the defect this cycle's evaluator named: every path this contract's own `evidence`/`red_evidence`/`green_evidence` fields cite must be reachable from the Outputs table, and it now is; that prior convention is superseded, not repeated. `unit-tests`/`acceptance-tests` `green_evidence` now points at the re-captured 65/0 focused-tests-{sh,ps1}.log (content re-measured, path unchanged); `red_evidence` still points at red-undermatched-capability-{sh,ps1}.log (path unchanged, content re-captured, no longer crashing). Two survivors the evaluator classed Minor were left open, per instruction: MUT-7 (`_required_facets` ignoring the matched set) survives because both fixture Capabilities already match; MUT-9 (truncating `_iter_warn_nodes` per evidence tree) survives because the multi-node WARN fixture scales nodes by component, confounding "per node" with "per component" -- neither is closed by this pass.
